At least in one place I see refine ⟨x, ?_⟩ being used where use x would suffice. Not sure how common this is yet.

To my (mild) surprise, use hP can be used to refine a hP ∧ hQ goal to hQ, though I don't think this is idiomatic.
For a ∃ (or something definitionally equivalent to a ∃, like x ∈ range S i.e. ∃ x' ∈ S, x = x', if I recalled correctly), then surely a use would be more idiomatic.

Not that Tau Ceti is too concerned with code quality, but items such as this one seems like free improvement (can be checked deterministically).

Thoughts?

Yes!

The best option here is to write a linter, and PR it to Mathlib and include it in the standard set. That then gives this cleanup to everyone, and Tau Ceti will just automatically adapt.

Cheaper and lazier is just a PR to Tau Ceti cleaning up all current instances.

I would discourage adding review or authoring prompting about this. It's an expensive and cumbersome way to get the result!
I personally do not think the example you gave is unidiomatic, in my mental model use is literally defined as the refine statement you gave

I agree,

  • refine is in core but use needs mathlib, so (hypothesis) is more likely to be understood
  • refine ⟨x, ?_, ?_⟩ lets you name multiple goals at once, so using the same pattern for the special case of only one, reduces the amount to remember

Looking for precedents in mathlib4.

  • There's a pull request (ironically by @Kim Morrison :thinking: but prepared with Claude Code, so it may merely reflect Claude's habit…) (https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/39844/files#diff-b63de0261ba5ce5f92b71f58289696d866e1d19da75b19dbe434e78f14e1f7cdR483-R502) that changes the use (or constructor) to refine. Other cases changing use to refine are much weaker, since the refine can replace two or three tactic invocations, so refine would be shorter (nonstraightforward proof golfing?). For example https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/22915/files#diff-d96f9794fe1c1b96bdf6b5053dc86a59ba405c71f4d7a4899b5b4446c7f959b8L92-R126 or https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/43056/files#diff-3c09e8c4132a7078555472e69466d46bf247bba49ccde0a4b8b4269799be1655L105-R104 .
  • In the opposite direction (change refine to use), there's a pull request https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/32643/files#diff-96b6e72cf5cfbce0d9769567f865deee21ffacd9f789d12af598953a6b6da7ebL229-R230 (looks like straightforward proof golfing).
Perhaps a less “controversial” case is apply f.mpr instead of rw [f], and apply f.mp instead of rw [← f]. Assume f has the form p ↔ q.

Both of these are valid IMO

Side note: why is the title of this thread seemingly about a famous musician?

Seems like not everyone agrees on the refine linter rule above. Thought about having these linter rules instead?

  • Never use (congrArg (fun ...) hf), use congr(... $...) instead
  • Don't use def for functions returning a typeclass, use instance instead (unless it's intentional to hide this function from implicit instance synthesis, possibly because of performance reason. Need to figure out an appropriate criteria here)
  • Do not have redundant let := ... or have := ... when they're not used or otherwise instance synthesis already work to deduce these
  • Simplify by exact expr to expr

More generally: it's indeed true that it's better to have the linter in mathlib than here, but it takes much effort to write and review a linter, and if a linter improves code quality _now_ then it's better to have it than not. Which is an argument to have temporary Tau Ceti-only linters. Thoughts?

There's also the question of should linter need human review. (The reason why linters are needed in the first place is that the agents don't “know” what is good code, so it feel like agent review can't really work for reviewing whether a linter is a good idea.)
